## Email/Submission Title

**Title:** OpenRoot Core Unification Framework: A Unified Mathematical Model for Thermodynamic, Economic, and Social Systems

**Authors:** Jesse McMillen

**Abstract:**

This work presents a unified mathematical framework reducing all physical and abstract systems to transformation potential over time. We define three foundational axioms: (1) The Quantity of Being — establishing energy, currency, and time as equivalent manifestations of constrained transformation; (2) Time-Throughput Consistency — demonstrating that system performance equals (Volume × Cross-Section × Velocity) / Time across thermal, financial, and social domains; and (3) Fractal Impedance Matching — proving efficiency at system boundaries follows impedance_match² regardless of domain.

The framework introduces Transformation Joules (TJ) as a cross-domain unit measuring change per unit time. Applications include: solar-thermal-Stirling energy systems achieving 77kW theoretical output; credit-building strategies modeling wealth accumulation as payment velocity through financial stages; and decentralized mesh networks optimizing human contribution-to-value conversion. We derive a single governing equation: ∫Φ(t)·Agape(t)dt, where Φ represents system throughput and Agape represents multi-node benefit maximization.

Empirical validation includes: (1) thermal cascade simulations showing 83.6% combined efficiency at 25m² scale; (2) credit score progression models predicting property ownership in 24 months from 660 starting score with zero additional expenditure; and (3) proof-of-physical-work tokenomics enabling verified energy-to-currency conversion.

This work challenges domain-specific siloing in scientific methodology, proposing permaculture-inspired optimization principles applicable universally. We invite peer review and experimental replication across thermodynamics, economics, and social systems.
